Connecting WhatsApp

Connecting your WhatsApp number

Connect your WhatsApp number to Hermes so the AI replies on it.

Before you start

  • Admin access to your Meta Business portfolio, and to developers.facebook.com inside it.
  • A phone number that has never had WhatsApp — a fresh SIM, eSIM, or virtual number. A physical SIM or eSIM is most reliable.
  • The verify token from 41 Labs.
  • Access to your Hermes workspace Settings.
  • About 30 to 45 minutes.

Step by step

01

Create your Meta App

Sign in to developers.facebook.com inside your Business, then open Create App.

  1. Choose the Connect on WhatsApp use case.
  2. Set the integration type to Integrate with API.
  3. Enter the app name and a contact email.
  4. Link the app to your Meta Business portfolio, then Create app.

Create Meta app — App details: name and contact email.

Use cases — select Connect with customers through WhatsApp.

Overview — review, then Create app.

02

Copy the app secret

Open the app dashboard, then Settings → Basic.

  1. Next to App secret, click Show.
  2. Copy the secret and store it with your Hermes credentials.

The app secret is unique to this app. It signs the inbound webhooks, and Hermes uses it to validate every message from this number. Never paste it into logs or tickets.

App settings → Basic — App ID and App secret (click Show to reveal).

03

Point the webhook at Hermes

Open WhatsApp → Configuration (or Basic setup → Step 2. Production setup → Webhooks).

The callback URL — routing is by Phone Number ID:

https://aisalescloser.41labs.ai/api/webhook/whatsapp
  1. Paste the callback URL above.
  2. Paste the verify token from 41 Labs.
  3. Click Verify and save.
  4. Under Webhook fields, open Manage and subscribe to messages.

Saving the URL and subscribing fields are two separate actions. If Verify and save fails, the token is not live yet on the Hermes side — tell 41 Labs before you retry.

Configure webhook — Callback URL and Verify token, then Verify and save.

Webhook fields — subscribe to messages.

04

Add your phone number

In Step 2. Production setup, open Register your WhatsApp phone number, create your WABA, then Add number.

  1. Fill the WhatsApp Business profile: display name, timezone, category.
  2. Add a description if you want one.

The number must never have had WhatsApp on it. A personal number fails with "already registered" — either delete it from the WhatsApp app first (one-way; this wipes that account and the number becomes bot-only) or use a fresh SIM, eSIM, or virtual number. WhatsApp blocks many VoIP numbers, so a physical SIM or eSIM is most reliable.

05

Verify the number with the code

Choose Text message or Phone call, then enter the one-time code.

06

Register the number and record its IDs

The number shows Not registered. Register it, then record its two IDs.

  1. Click Register and set a 6-digit two-step PIN. Store the PIN.
  2. Wait for the status to flip to Registered.
  3. Turn the Subscribe webhooks toggle ON for this WABA.
WABA IDThe WhatsApp Business account ID.
Phone Number IDThe inbound routing key that maps a message to your workspace.

These are IDs, not secrets. You paste both into Hermes in Step 11.

Registered number — green badge, WABA ID and Phone Number ID, Subscribe webhooks on.

07

Generate the permanent access token

Open Send message → Step 1: Generate token, then Generate token.

  1. Copy the token once and store it safely. Meta shows it a single time.

This is the access token Hermes needs. It must carry whatsapp_business_messaging (send and receive) and whatsapp_business_management (so the wizard can list the numbers). An empty number list later means the management permission is missing.

Skip Meta's own "Step 2: Send message" test. Hermes is the send path — the QR code and curl panel below the button are Meta's test harness, not part of this setup.

Generate token — the QR and Send panel below it is Meta's test harness (skip it).

08

Give the system user access to the real WABA

A valid token is not the same as access. The token can be valid, permanent, and list the messaging scope and still fail to send with OAuthException code 100. Meta auto-creates a sandbox "Test WhatsApp Business Account" and often assigns only that one — your real number's WABA is not assigned by default, so inbound works but every outbound send returns 400.

Assign the real WABA to the system user:

  1. Open Business Settings → Users → System Users and select your user.
  2. Click ⋯ → Assign assets → WhatsApp accounts.
  3. Select your real WABA — not Test WhatsApp Business Account.
  4. Enable Messages (or Full access → Everything), then Assign assets.

Confirm the real WABA now shows under WhatsApp accounts · Full access, alongside the test one. If only the test account is there, outbound will keep failing.

Assign assets — select your real WABA and turn on Messages (or Full access → Everything).

Result — the real WABA under WhatsApp accounts · Full access, alongside the test one.

09

Add a payment method — only before going live

Skip this for testing. Inbound AI replies are service conversations: 1,000 free per month, no payment method needed.

Add a payment method only before business-initiated messages — templates, follow-ups, campaigns — or before going live.

10

Connect the number in Hermes

Open your Hermes workspace Settings → Meta connect wizard.

  1. Paste the token (Step 7) and WABA ID (Step 6).
  2. When the wizard lists the numbers, pick your number.
  3. Let the wizard subscribe the app to the WABA, save, and run its test.

A green result means the connection is live. The wizard has subscribed your app to the WABA for you.

11

Confirm the AI replies end-to-end

Send a WhatsApp message to the number from your own phone.

The message reaches Hermes, passes the webhook signature check, is matched to your workspace by Phone Number ID, and the AI replies.

Nothing arrives? Check in this order:

  1. The system user is missing the real WABA (Step 8 — the usual culprit).
  2. The app secret or verify token is not live on the Hermes side.
  3. The messages field is not subscribed (Step 3).
  4. The app is not subscribed to the WABA (re-run Step 10).
